scope: Untimed software/DSP and native-JSBSim checks. No physical route, listening, acoustic or performance qualification.
cause: The fan wake switched to full idle base gain whenever N1 exceeded 0.01 percent; the fan tone also had a nonzero base. F135 N1 turns with N2 during native starter motoring. Combustion was false and not the source of the early static.
change: Below the profile idle N1, fan tones receive r=clamp01(N1/idleN1), wake receives r^2. Existing N2^2 gain and native fuel/running combustion decision remain. At or above idle these added multipliers equal one. No new sources, filters, memory or setup ABI fields.
acceptance: At N1=N2=0.1 percent, standalone engine output peak is below 1e-4 in both aircraft and all three audible tiers.
Across each low-speed decade (0.01, 0.1, 1 percent) wake amplitude falls by more than 50x; no constant floor remains.
F135 pre-lightoff core whine follows 5/10/14 percent N2 at 190/380/532 Hz, 44.1/48 kHz, all tiers; tone RMS exceeds separated wake by at least 4x.

A real cold native F135 start has zero fuel/thrust and combustion false at initial N2 below 0.1 percent and at 10 percent motoring, then fueled combustion before running. Captured initial rotation, motoring, first-lightoff and running states replay through all three tiers.

Eight legacy SF50 Low/Med reference fixtures are bit-identical in both channels over the settled 0.4-0.8 second window; retained whole-output changes are restricted to initial sub-idle smoothing and downstream filter tails.
